gloss: to catch one's eye; to come into view

definitions.gloss: to catch one's eye; to come into view; to be seen
definitions.explanation: Of something seen: to come into one's field of vision, usually without being looked for. The thing seen is the subject, marked with が.

examples.japanese: ⟦{看板|かんばん}→看板：00166_kanban⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{目|め}に{入|はい}った。
⟦{窓|まど}→窓：02254_mado⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{富士山|ふじさん}→富士山：09514_fujisan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{目|め}に{入|はい}る。
examples.english: When you open the window, Mount Fuji comes into view.

examples.japanese: ⟦{忙|いそが}しくて→忙しい：00591_isogashii⟧、⟦{周|まわ}り→周り：01732_mawari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧{目|め}に{入|はい}らなかった。
examples.english: I was so busy that I didn't notice anything around me.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
- X⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{目|め}に{入|はい}る: X catches one's eye
- ⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧{目|め}に{入|はい}らない: to notice nothing else (absorbed in something)
- {目|め}に{入|はい}れて⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{痛|いた}くない→痛い：01108_itai⟧: to dote on (a child or grandchild); literally 'would not hurt even if put in one's eye'

WATCH OUT:
The phrase is also used literally: ⟦{砂|すな}→砂：00890_suna⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{目|め}に{入|はい}った means 'I got sand in my eye.' Context decides which reading is meant.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{目|め}につく→目につく：18062_menitsuku⟧: to be noticeable, to stand out; stresses that the thing is conspicuous, often unpleasantly so
- ⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧: to be visible; neutral about whether one notices
